newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Steady rates, data to drive Bel-20 higher still.
newsitem.headline: Steady rates, data to drive Bel-20 higher still.

text.p: Belgian shares moved further into uncharted territory on Friday, boosted by the Dow Jones's .DJI rise and a batch of supportive late trades linked to the expiry of Bel-20 futures and options.
"Interest rates are not likely to rise, economic indicators show no danger for high inflation, both in the U.S. and in Europe. This helped push up the index," a trader said.

Dealers forecast the Bel-20 could rise further after ending up 14.07 points or 0.76 percent, at 1,869.48, its fourth consecutive all-time high. Volume was heavy, closing at 4.06 billion francs (Belgian shares only).

Pharmaceuticals and chemicals firm UCB rose further, ending up 3.29 percent at 78,500 francs amid optimism that the company would push ahead into the Japanese market after its promotional tour around the world.
Insurer Fortis AG rose 95 francs or 2.0 percent to 4,835, reflecting Europe-wide confidence in the insurance sector.
Cement producer CBR edged up 2.22 percent to 2,535 francs, discount retailer Colruyt gained 1.42 percent to 14,300 francs and transporter CMB
Dealers added that many investors were picking up shares in these companies in last minute trading.
Traders said some investors had already started returning to European stock exchanges, moving out of the United States as 1997 corporate profits there looked set to be less attractive than in 1996.
But in the next few weeks Belgium could see some consolidation, one trader said.
"The (Belgian) market needs some rest as does the U.S. one, so we might see some slowdown towards the end of the year," he said.
